title: Book 7 — Polymnia, Chapter 58
paragraphs: Meanwhile the fleet was sailing out of the Hellespont and coasting along in the opposite direction from the land army, for the fleet was making west toward the promontory of Sarpedon, to which it had been previously ordered to go and wait for the army. The land army meanwhile was marching east, toward the sunrise, through the Chersonese, keeping on its right the tomb of Helle the daughter of Athamas, and on its left the city of Cardia, passing through the middle of a town called Agora. From there, bending around the Gulf of Melas and crossing the river Melas (whose stream did not suffice for the army at that time and ran dry), the army — having crossed this river, from which the gulf also takes its name — went westward, passing the Aeolian city of Aenus and the lake Stentoris, until at last it arrived at Doriscus.
